memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD
hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go out of his
country." - Ex 11:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Chapter 11 closes with a summary, and it is not a triumphant one. Moses and
Aaron did everything God asked. All the wonders, all the warnings, all the
standing before an angry king. And the closing line is: Pharaoh would not let
them go.

Imagine being Moses at this point. By every visible measure, the mission has
failed. Ten confrontations, and the people are still slaves.

But we know what Moses did not yet know. The very next chapter brings the
Passover and the Exodus. The night was darkest just before God moved.

There is a lesson here for anyone doing faithful work with nothing to show for
it. The parent praying for a child who is not changing. The believer sharing
Christ with a friend who will not listen. The servant of God labouring in a
place that seems barren. Moses' obedience was not wasted simply because the
result had not arrived yet.

Paul writes, "Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we
will reap a harvest if we do not give up" (Gal 6:9). Notice the phrase: at the
proper time. Not our time. His.

Faithfulness is measured by obedience, not by outcome.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to give up because nothing seems to be changing?
2. Can you define faithfulness today by obedience rather than results?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to keep doing what You have asked even when I see no results. My
job is obedience; the harvest belongs to You. Amen.
